video_title: Is it Victor Wembanyama’s league now?! 👀 Game 1 of the WCF: Spurs vs. OKC | Howdy Partners

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's unprecedented playoff performance and unique skills
quotes.excerpt: Every time you see Victor Wembanyama play, you're likely to see something that you have never seen before.
quotes.quote: Wemby was twice as good as anybody else on that floor last night, Mike. Dude, I don't know how do we even put this into perspective? I guess I'll start here. Every time you see Victor Wembanyama play, you're likely to see something that you have never seen before. And there were several of those moments last night. It was that kind of performance last night. We've never seen somebody that young go for 40 points and 20 rebounds in a playoff game. He had 41 and 24. We've never seen a seven-and-a-half-foot guy knock down a 30-foot shot that his team absolutely needed to be able to send a game into double overtime.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's incredible and easy-looking finishes
quotes.excerpt: I've never seen a seven-and-a-half-foot guy sense a double team coming, spin to the inside.
quotes.quote: Some of the plays that he made, some of the finishes, I've never seen a seven-and-a-half-foot guy sense a double team coming, spin to the inside and just make a hook shot in the lane with his left hand, his off-hand, look easy. Mike, I don't know about you, but there were a bunch of times last night, I just had my hands on my head in complete awe of what we were watching.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's performance as a culmination of his skills and desire to perform
quotes.excerpt: A lot of the footwork, the spins, the, hey, double team coming, I don't care. I can shoot over it.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Absolutely, my man, and a lot of what we saw was just sort of a culmination of everything he sort of put together from his time, like his first day in the league, and you saw a lot of his Hakeem Olajuwon stuff. A lot of the footwork, the spins, the, hey, double team coming, I don't care. I can shoot over it, or I'll go in between it and dunk. It was, you know what? I'm going back to my old-school sports writing roots, but last night was one of those nights where you really wanted to take just take a bead and really process everything you saw and just do your best to encapsulate that moment, you know, with whatever, whatever you write. And I was kind of regretful that I didn't really get to do that the way I wanted to, because you know, we got a million things going on. But I did my best, my man, and hopefully we got a lot more of these coming. I think we do. And I think it's going to be on both sides.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs and OKC are starting a long-term epic rivalry
quotes.excerpt: I think this is going to be a long, epic series, and this is going to be the start of what's going to be an epic rivalry.
quotes.quote: And that's the thing. We got, I think this is going to be a long, epic series, and this is going to be start, or it is the start, of what's going to be an epic rivalry. I think over the next 10 years, we might get seven or eight of these series between these teams. And if you're anybody else in the Western Conference watching this series, I think two words come to mind. O is the first one, and I'm not allowed to say the next one on a Disney platform. But because the level for these teams is just so high, and they are ascending.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's unique blend of athleticism, skill, and competitive drive
quotes.excerpt: Wemby does have a very rare competitiveness for somebody who's that gifted, a superstar.
quotes.quote: And Wemby is ascending. I ran into somebody with the Spurs last night in the hallway, and it was a pretty giddy hallway outside that visitor's locker room. He said, 'Man, he's just a baby.' Dude, this guy's going to keep getting better. He's going to keep getting stronger. He's going to keep working on his skill set. And of all the ways that Wemby's unique, and again, like we've never seen anybody that tall who's that athletic. We've never seen anybody that tall who's that skilled. We certainly have never seen anybody who's all of those things combined. But the competitiveness of this guy is unique. Like somebody who, and it's not unprecedented. A lot of the stuff with Wemby's unprecedented, but Wemby does have a very rare competitiveness for somebody who's that gifted, a superstar who's that determined to squeeze every bit of potential out of his game. And he takes things personally too, Mike.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's personal drive to be the league's best and embrace clutch moments
quotes.excerpt: Wemby had made very, very clear he believed belonged to him. And this series is an opportunity for Wemby to stake his claim as the best player in the league.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: There was a pregame trophy ceremony, the MVP trophy, the trophy that Wemby had made very, very clear he believed belonged to him. And this series is a lot of things. One of them is an opportunity for Wemby to stake his claim as the best player in the league. Basically, for him to say, 'Hey, it's my league now.' It's a 1-0 lead, it ain't four, but that was a hell of a step last night doing that.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: It was, man. And, you know, we all, me included, we all will probably overreact a little bit to Game 1. But man, that performance, it was like Mitch Johnson said after the game, that it was sort of, he said that he's got this unique desire to want to step into those moments. And, you know, a lot of young players, they shy away from that.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's 30-foot shot rivaled Stephen Curry's iconic moment
quotes.excerpt: The Steph shot in regular season games is one of the iconic shots of this generation. That Wemby shot was pretty iconic.
quotes.quote: It was from almost the same spot on the floor. Steph was a little further out, but it was that same, it was going the same direction in the same building, very near the same spot, and he is, I don't know, 15 inches taller than Steph. The Steph shot in regular season games is one of the iconic shots of this generation. That Wemby shot was pretty iconic. And what's crazy is, I, it was his most ridiculous highlight of overtime, but he had a reel.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's powerful dunk, late-game scoring, and impactful defense
quotes.excerpt: He outscored the Thunder 12-7 to close the game. To close out a 41-point, 24-rebound, three-block performance.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: And one of those was that and-one dunk where Chet came over and tried to challenge, and he dunked it with some real force. I'm going to say some real animosity. He didn't like Chet swatting him at the regulation buzzer, sending it into OT. And man, to have that kind of a dagger dunk. The man had six dunks in the game. I think three of them were in the overtime periods. From the time he let that 30-whatever-footer go, Mike, he outscored the Thunder 12-7 to close the game. To close out a 41-point, 24-rebound, three-block performance, and the three blocks does not even begin to hint at the impact that he made on the defensive end.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: That last block though, that was like the topper. Like you blocked J-Dub at the rim, and it's a dad block. It's, you didn't give it to me.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's dramatic flair and ability to thrive under pressure
quotes.excerpt: He wants to be the best player ever, and he wants to be recognized as the best player ever.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Oh, no, you do that, and then you strut over to the corner where your bench is, and he basically poses for your teammate.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Hey, yeah, I forgot about. He was just like.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Yeah. And that, I mean, listen, the guy has a flair for the dramatic. Like I said, he wants to squeeze every potential. He wants to be the best player ever, and he wants to be recognized as the best player ever. He wants, he loves the stage, he loves these lights. That's why, that's part of the reason why going into this, and we'll see, you know, maybe, maybe this could end up getting proven wrong as the series goes, but one reason I wasn't too concerned about playoff inexperience is because we've seen Wemby on big stages, and we've seen how much he responds to the bright lights. We're seeing that right now.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Keldon Johnson on the Spurs' 'double down' mentality in hostile environments
quotes.excerpt: We didn't come here to try to steal one in Oklahoma City. We came to win.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Yeah, yeah. It's just not, it's not just Vic, it's all those guys. I was talking to Keldon after the game, Keldon Johnson, and he was just like, because I asked him, I said, 'Man, like in an environment like this, when that crowd starts going crazy, you know, like what, what's the mentality? What's the mindset there?' He was like, 'Double down.' He's like, 'Double down because when you play against,' and he said, 'We got all the respect in the world for Oklahoma City. But when you play like a, when you play against a team like this and an environment like this, when they come with that energy, if you don't match it, you're going to get your, you know what, beat.' And he said, 'All due respect to Oklahoma City, but we didn't come here to try to steal one in Oklahoma City. We came to win.' And I was like, 'Okay, that's what y'all are on.' And that permeates throughout the entire roster, and it's just, it's, I guess it's a credit to the GM, Brian Wright, for building that team that way, because, you know, you've got, when you kind of look throughout that roster, you've got some alpha dogs, whether that's Steph, Vic, and Keldon.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: And Harper's an alpha dog, my friend.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' roster is built with a few key 'alpha dogs' leading the team
quotes.excerpt: You don't have to have a whole team full of them. You just need three or four, and the rest of the team is going to follow.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Oh, yeah.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: You got to get to that later. But when you, you don't have to have a whole team full of them. You just need three or four, and the rest of the team is going to follow, they're going to follow right behind. And I think that's what they've got. They've got a ton of like just super competitive people. Like, you know, like these guys competed everything. I mean, you should see some of the things they're doing in the locker room. It's, it's wild, but credit to them, but Oklahoma City is not done.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's history of overcoming Game 1 losses and problem-solving in playoff series
quotes.excerpt: One of the things he loves about his team is their problem-solving, their ability to figure out how to attack problems.
quotes.quote: Oh, God, no, listen. OKC, they've been through this. They lost Game 1 at home to the Nuggets last year. They lost Game 1 at home on a heartbreaking game-winner by Tyrese Haliburton in the NBA Finals. Those were both seven-game series, they won both those series. As Mark Daigneault said, one of the things he loves about his team is their problem-solving, their ability to figure out how to attack problems, how to address issues throughout the course of games and really throughout the course of series. They take a lot of pride in being able to get better game by game by game in a series.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's defensive presence created a 'one-man zone' and intimidated Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.excerpt: Wemby is essentially a one-man zone. He basically clogs up everything inside the three-point line by himself.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Now, as Shai told me the other night, Wemby presents problems that nobody else does. And one of the problems he presents, I would say probably as awesome as he was offensively last night, defensively is where the Spurs really won the game, and that is Wemby is essentially a one-man zone. He basically clogs up everything inside the three-point line by himself. And they've got great point-of-attack defenders. Steph Castle, Dylan Harper, those two dudes in particular. And they're throwing extra bodies at Shai, and Shai went 7-for-23. I mean, he made it very clear after getting that MVP trophy, he didn't play up to that standard, and he pinned the blame on himself for the loss. He basically said, 'I have to be better, especially against a team of this caliber.' He understands the weight when you lift that trophy. He understands the weight that comes with that, he understands the responsibility that comes with that. And 7-for-23 shooting, he had 12 assists, but four turnovers, not good enough. He did finally, you know, kind of find, he basically, he didn't use the word intimidate, but he did admit, like Wemby intimidated him. It was an intimidating factor. He talked about needing to find the balance between aggressive and being smart attacking when Wemby's back there. And he found that for like the last, it was the last 5:26 of the fourth quarter when they came back, they rallied. He had 10 points and a couple assists during that stretch. The crazy thing, Caruso had the game of his life. Caruso knocked down eight threes. A lot of them were open because of the way that Wemby was playing. But the Spurs will take that. Like, 'Hey, if Alex Caruso's jump shot's going to beat us, and Shai's going to have a hard time,' the Spurs will take that every single time.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: That's the thing though. Like you could tell that San Antonio sort of devoted everything to, you know, just sort of neutralizing Shai. But Shai, just for the numbers and everything, and him talking about how he didn't play well enough, he played okay. He was okay.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander are expected to improve their shooting in future games
quotes.excerpt: Shai is not going to miss shots like that all series. The Oklahoma City Thunder, they're not going to be standing back there with wide open shots and miss those shots.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: 7-for-23 is not going to cut it. We don't have the soft pedal things for him. He's a grown man.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: No, that's not what I'm saying. What I'm saying is Shai is not going to miss shots like that all series. The Oklahoma City Thunder, they're not going to be standing back there with wide open shots and miss those shots the way that they did in Game 1. They missed a bunch of shots that they knocked down fairly easily.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC must find ways to move Wembanyama out of the paint to create offensive opportunities
quotes.excerpt: They've got to figure out ways to move the defense and especially move Wemby.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I didn't think Shai was getting great looks. I, I thought that because of Wemby's presence, Shai, and Wemby's presence, and they were throwing extra bodies at him. If Shai, like operating at the top of the offense, he's got, he's got a great point-of-attack defender on him, then it's guys on the elbows, guys in the box, one of them on the box is Victor Wembanyama. The defense is loaded up against him. They've got to figure out ways to move the defense and especially move Wemby. They've got to get Wemby moved.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: You got to get him out of the paint.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Well, out of the paint or even moving inside the paint. I forgot who, who got the bucket, but there was one time where they got a drive and Chet was able to set a Gortat screen. They've got to get him moving, can't just let him be back there playing goalie. That's just, that's not going to work. But whatever it is, Shai understands the weight of the crown, and it's especially heavy when you've got a seven-and-a-half-foot alien trying to rip it out of your hands.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's high ankle sprain is a significant factor, but OKC believes they have solutions
quotes.excerpt: They did play that game without De'Aaron Fox. That's one more guy that can give you problems on both ends of the floor.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Oh, no doubt. But like I felt like he made, for the most part, he made the right plays. He actually made some pretty good plays. He saw some things and hit the guys that he needed to hit. They just couldn't make those shots. I'm really, like I said, I just think that Oklahoma City is going to be much better. And you know how it is, man, once you sort of, the first game or two is like you're feeling each other out, trying to figure out what you're trying to do. And if that is how they are going to, to play, OKC, I think they've got solutions for that. And then it becomes a matter of, okay, how do they defend the Spurs? Because, let's be real here, they did play that game without De'Aaron Fox. That's one more guy that can give you problems on both ends of the floor, and he was.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: And Fox has an ankle issue. I think they're calling it stiffness, it's a sprain.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it's a high sprain.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I was going to say, it ain't a low sprain.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's Game 1 absence was precautionary, and his ankle injury will need management throughout the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: It's not going to get any better with him playing. I think it's a matter of trying to manage it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: So what are you hearing about his potential availability in Game 2 or moving forward in the series first?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Well, it sounded like his absence from Game 1, for the most part, was pretty precautionary. I think D could have.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I don't know about precautionary in Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: I'm telling you, man, like when you, when you got horses like that, you know, you can, you can keep one in the stable and still feel good about your chances. I think they want to get that ankle, because it's a, it's one of those deals where it's not going to get any better with him playing.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: That's what Mitch Johnson basically said, 'He's dealing with this as long as we're playing.'

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Yeah. And so I think it's a matter of trying to manage it. Because say you get through this series, you got another tough one coming.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The young Spurs, led by Dylan Harper's historic performance, are a terrifying ascending talent
quotes.excerpt: The youngest starting lineup in a conference finals game, which means as far as back as they can track.
quotes.quote: Well, you got to throw all the bullets you can, you know, you got to get through this series because OKC is a historically elite team, a defending championship team, you know, you took home court advantage, but they're still the number one seed. Now, Dylan Harper, what a response though. 24 points, first playoff start, 24 points, 11 rebounds, seven steals, six assists. The only other rookie to go 20 points, 10 rebounds, five and five in a playoff game, Magic Johnson. And Mike, you don't have Fox, who's kind of, you know, he's your vet closer. He's not an old vet, but he's a vet. The average age of that starting lineup for the Spurs, 22.9 years old. I think I saw that was the, what was that, the youngest starting lineup in a conference finals game, which means as far as back as they can track. And, you know, again, that's, that's what is so terrifying about the Spurs. Their seven-and-a-half-foot alien who wants all the smoke is an ascending talent. He's going to keep getting better, he's going to keep getting stronger, he's going to keep working on his game. Dylan Harper's just scratching the surface. Steph Castle, who did a lot of good, also did a lot of bad, 11 turnovers, but he had one of his trampoline dunks over SGA when he just goes up off two feet in traffic off a drive. He's an ascending talent. I mean, Carter Bryant is, is getting key minutes. They're just so loaded already with the arrow pointing up on almost their entire, at least their entire rotation.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Sean Sweeney's defensive tactics, aided by Wembanyama's presence, stifled OKC's offense
quotes.excerpt: Sean Sweeney's in charge of that defense, and man, that, it's nice to have a tool in the toolbox like Victor Wembanyama.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: And Mike, I also want to point out, look, the last superstar to send the Thunder home in a playoff series was Luka Doncic. But the last defensive tactician to send the Thunder home in a playoff series was Sean Sweeney, who left Dallas last summer to become the Spurs' associate head coach. He'll be the first to tell you, Mitch Johnson is one hell of a head coach, and Mitch is in charge of the, you know, the big picture stuff. I think part of the reason this team is so mature beyond their years is the way that he empowers them and the way that he challenges them. He's in charge of the offense, which, you know, it's, it's been awfully good for a team that doesn't necessarily have a lot of traditional shooting. But Sean Sweeney's in charge of that defense, and man, that, it's nice to have a tool in the toolbox like Victor Wembanyama.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: The one-man zone, yeah.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Yeah, but that defensive plan really gave the Thunder and SGA in particular a lot of problems. And as much as SGA struggled, a lot of the credit goes to the Spurs' defense, and honestly, a lot of it goes to Wemby just because, Mike, he makes guys just not want to go in the paint. How many times have guys, no, not going in there. Let me, let me dribble through, let me just, you know, put it in reverse. But again, a great game plan by the Spurs, great execution by the Spurs on that end, and a great challenge for OKC to try to figure out how do you attack that?

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Both teams displayed an incredible will to win in an all-time great game
quotes.excerpt: Neither one of those teams was budging, man. That was one of the best overall team performances on both sides.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Agreed. But let's, let's, let's give both teams their flowers here, because we talk about all the cliché stuff about, you know, just the will to win and all that stuff. And neither one of those teams was budging, man. They were, that was, that's probably one of the best just overall team performances on both sides that I've seen with my own eyes. I mean.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: It was an all-time great game.
